questions.question: A man spends 40% of his monthly salary on house rent. If every month, he also spends ₹442 on conveyance and ₹9,115 on grocery and saves the remaining ₹946, his monthly salary is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Monthly Salary** be 100%.

**Expenditure on Rent** = 40%

**Remaining Salary** = 100% − 40% = 60%

This 60% equals the sum of **Conveyance**, **Grocery**, and **Savings**.

60% = ₹442 + ₹9,115 + ₹946 = ₹10,503

100% = (₹10,503 ÷ 60) × 100 = ₹17,505

**∴ The correct answer is ₹17,505.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ed96c1be87c1bc7581ca3484c37460a49fa80554a6ecb672fdbcbd782c9433a7.png] 

**Given:**

**Rent Expenditure** = 40% of Salary

**Conveyance** = ₹442

**Grocery** = ₹9,115

**Savings** = ₹946

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total non-rent amount = ₹(442 + 9,115 + 946)

⇒ Total non-rent amount = ₹10,503

⇒ Let total salary be S.

⇒ S − 40% of S = ₹10,503

⇒ 60% of S = ₹10,503

⇒ (60 ÷ 100) × S = 10,503

⇒ S = (10,503 × 100) ÷ 60

⇒ S = 10,503 × (5 ÷ 3)

⇒ S = 3,501 × 5 = ₹17,505

**∴ The correct answer is ₹17,505.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Expenditure

Total Income is always considered 100%. Total Income = Savings + Total Expenditure.

Successive Percentage

If spending is done on the **remaining** amount, use the formula: Final = Initial × (100−r₁)/100 × (100−r₂)/100.

Base Change Rule

When calculating percentage increase/decrease, always ensure the **denominator (base)** corresponds to the original value.

questions.question: Due to decrease in manpower, the production in a factory decreases by 12%. By what percentage (rounded off to two decimal places) should the working hours be increased to restore the original production?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To restore original value after a decrease of r%, increase required = [r ÷ (100 − r)] × 100

Here, decrease r = 12%

Required increase % = [12 ÷ (100 − 12)] × 100

Required increase % = (12 ÷ 88) × 100 = 13.6363...

**∴ The correct answer is 13.64%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Decrease in **production** = 12%

**Formula:** Production = **Manpower** × **Working Hours**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/42c16e2ada0ec158b98daf58835f434ec304a11b08a847eaa86902c844cc63a9.png] 

⇒ Let original production be 100 units.

⇒ New production after 12% decrease = 100 − 12 = 88 units.

⇒ To restore original production (100), we must increase 88 units by (100 − 88) = 12 units.

⇒ Percentage increase required = (12 ÷ 88) × 100

⇒ Percentage increase required = (3 ÷ 22) × 100 = 300 ÷ 22

⇒ Percentage increase required = 13.6363... ≈ 13.64%

**∴ The correct answer is 13.64%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Stability Rule

If the product of two variables is constant, an increase in one by x% requires a decrease in the other by [x ÷ (100 + x)] × 100%.

Base Change Concept

When a value is decreased and then increased to the original, the **base** for the increase is the **new decreased value**, not the original value.

Successive Percentage Change

The overall change for two successive changes of a% and b% is given by [a + b + (a × b)/100]%.</p

questions.question: A person who spends 75% of his monthly income is able to save ₹5,538 per month. His monthly expenses (in ₹) are:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Savings %** = 100% − 75% = 25%

According to the question, 25% = ₹5,538

**Monthly Expenses** (75%) = 3 × 25%

**Monthly Expenses** = 3 × 5,538 = ₹16,614

**∴ The correct answer is ₹16,614.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b1c32236126368b69c87e400951616b695f923270d975d23a6a003e5883e533c.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Income = Expenditure + Savings

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **Total Income** be ₹x

⇒ Savings % = 100% − 75% = 25%

⇒ 25% of x = 5,538

⇒ (25/100) × x = 5,538

⇒ x/4 = 5,538

⇒ x = 5,538 × 4 = 22,152

⇒ Monthly Expenses = 75% of 22,152

⇒ Monthly Expenses = (3/4) × 22,152

⇒ Monthly Expenses = 3 × 5,538 = 16,614

**∴ The correct answer is ₹16,614.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

When income is taken as 100, any change in expenditure or savings directly translates to a change in the total base value.

Ratio Method

The ratio of Expenses to Savings is 75:25 or 3:1. If 1 unit represents ₹5,538, then 3 units represent the expenses.

Income Formula

Income = Savings ÷ (1 − Expense Rate). This helps in finding total income directly from savings and expense percentage.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

⇒ Let the **initial production** be 100 units.

⇒ After 20% **decrease**, new production = 100 − 20 = 80 units.

⇒ To restore original production, we need to **increase** from 80 back to 100.

⇒ Increase required = 100 − 80 = 20 units.

⇒ Percentage **increase in working hours** = (20 ÷ 80) × 100

⇒ Percentage increase = 1/4 × 100 = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

Product Stability Ratio

Commonly applied in **Price-Consumption** and **Time-Speed** problems where the total expenditure or distance remains fixed.

Successive Percentage

Net change for **successive** x% and y% is [x + y + (xy/100)]%.</p

questions.question: If 20% of k is 10 less than 1200% of 10, then k is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert **percentages** to decimals: 20% = 0.2 and 1200% = 12.

The equation becomes: 0.2 × k = (12 × 10) − 10

0.2k = 120 − 10 = 110

k = 110 ÷ 0.2 = 1100 ÷ 2 = 550

**∴ The correct answer is 550.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 20% of k = (1200% of 10) − 10

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b2aeef2ffe120a94d5dc9f7d10b99db04149ac21a12397288c90b21adb0263b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 20/100 × k = (1200/100 × 10) − 10

⇒ 1/5 × k = (12 × 10) − 10

⇒ k/5 = 120 − 10

⇒ k/5 = 110

⇒ k = 110 × 5

⇒ k = 550

**∴ The correct answer is 550.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To convert x% to a fraction, divide by 100: x/100. For example, 1200% = 1200/100 = 12.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage change = [(New Value − Original Value) ÷ Original Value] × 100.

A% of B property

A% of B is always equal to B% of A. This can simplify many mental calculations.</p

questions.question: Vipul spends 55% of his income. If he saves ₹18,000, then his income (in ₹) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Savings %** = 100% − **Expenditure %** = 100% − 55% = 45%

45% of **Income** = ₹18,000

1% of **Income** = 18,000 ÷ 45 = ₹400

100% (**Total Income**) = 400 × 100 = ₹40,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹40,000.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Expenditure** = 55% of Income

**Savings** = ₹18,000

**Formula Used:**

**Income** = **Expenditure** + **Savings**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4b5c0b5a64f188f85138474d00435a15beb013bc2f4ed4673a400b3653996e28.png] 

Let **Total Income** be 'I'.

⇒ **Savings** = I − (55% of I)

⇒ 18,000 = 45% of I

⇒ 18,000 = (45 ÷ 100) × I

⇒ I = (18,000 × 100) ÷ 45

⇒ I = 400 × 100

⇒ I = 40,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹40,000.**

**__Additional Information__**

Percentage Base Change

Income is always considered the 100% base. Any change in expenditure or savings is calculated relative to this 100%.

Savings Ratio

The ratio of **Expenditure** to **Savings** here is 55:45, which simplifies to 11:9. Using the unitary method, 9 units = ₹18,000, so 20 units (Total Income) = ₹40,000.

Successive Percentage

If income increases by x% and expenditure also changes, use the net effect formula: **New Income** = **Original Income** × (1 + x/100).

questions.question: The population of a town in 1930 was 3,48,000. If its population increased in two successive decades by 95% in each decade, the population of the town in 1950 was:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial **population** in 1930 = 3,48,000.

**Successive increase** of 95% for two decades (1930 to 1950).

Multiplying factor for 95% increase = (100 + 95)/100 = 1.95.

Final population = 3,48,000 × 1.95 × 1.95 = 3,48,000 × 3.8025.

Final population = 13,23,270.

**∴ The correct answer is 13,23,270.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Population in 1930 (P) = 3,48,000

Growth rate (r) = 95% per decade

Time period (n) = 1950 − 1930 = 2 decades

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/168baa145861bcfe519358f8a5b0103ddf228e915d46d379023fffcebbef40f5.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Final Population = P × (1 + r/100)ⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ Final Population = 3,48,000 × (1 + 95/100)²

⇒ Final Population = 3,48,000 × (1.95)²

⇒ Final Population = 3,48,000 × 3.8025

⇒ Final Population = 1,323,270

**∴ The correct answer is 13,23,270.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

If a value changes by x% and then by y% successively, the effective percentage change is given by [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

Population Growth Formula

Population after n years = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ, where P is initial population and r is the annual growth rate.

Population Decrease

If the population decreases by r% each year, the population after n years is P(1 − r/100)ⁿ.</p
